text:
Mina Patel: Quick heads-up — ran an nsys + perfetto pass on the 8k chat workload after the kernel-affinity change. Seeing a recurring pattern: short queue spikes right before matmul launches, then a long tail of small kernels. Putting notes here so we don't lose them.

Sachin Rao: Can you paste the timeline snippet? is it the queue_time that spikes or kernel launch latency? :thinking:

Mina Patel: It's mostly queue_time. Timeline -> GPU queue shows ~4-12ms spikes every ~40ms window. Compute blocks are ~6-8ms, so queuing is non-trivial. Perfetto export attached in the trace but here's a small excerpt: 
```
[GPU_QUEUE] 0.0 - 4.1ms  enqueue (prefix check)
[GPU_QUEUE] 44.0 - 56.8ms  enqueue (batch merge)  <- 12.8ms
[matmul_kernel] 56.9 - 63.7ms  (compute ~6.8ms)
[small_kernels x7] 63.8 - 75.9ms  (aggregate ~12ms)
```

Jordan Li: hmmm that merge point sounds like batch window boundary. What is continuous_batch_window_ms on that run?

Mina Patel: It was 12ms (default for this config). I toggled affinity to prefer cuBLAS matmul path on ptx_v2 which changed kernel selection, but didn't remove the enqueue spikes.

Sachin Rao: Two hypotheses: (1) batching window alignment + KV cache sweep causes microbursts of dispatch; (2) kernel selection changed the launch characteristics (more small kernels after matmul). Both increase visible queue.

Mina Patel: Agreed. I also saw KV cache maintenance logs at roughly the same cadence: 
```
[KVCacheSweeper] start=44.1ms dur=1.2ms keys=128
[KVCachePrefetch] start=44.3ms dur=0.6ms hits=102
```
Not enough to explain 12ms but might add jitter.

Jordan Li: Can you re-run with continuous_batch_window_ms=6 and batching.align_to_window=false? If the spikes are alignment artifacts they should smear out. Also try kernel_selector=prefer_single_kernel (disable split matmul).

Mina Patel: Re-ran with window=6 and selector=prefer_single_kernel. New timeline: queue spikes drop to ~2-4ms, matmul compute ~8ms, small_kernels reduced to x2. CPU -> GPU submission pattern is smoother.

Sachin Rao: Nice. So kernel split was causing many small post-kernel ops that clobbered the queue. That explains the long tail. Did you capture nsys export with cpu sampling?

Mina Patel: Yes. nsys command I used: 
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/run --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt -t cuda,osrt,nvtx --sample=cpu --capture-range=nvtx 
```
I also captured the CUDA kernel names and host call stacks.

Jordan Li: Can you run one more with perf counters (sm__* or l2) on a single GPU to see if launch contention or memory stalls dominate? use nsys with counters or nvprof fallback.

Mina Patel: Scheduled that. Early peek: sm_efficiency dips align with queue spikes, but mem_throughput steady. So likely kernel-launch contention + small-kernel overhead.

Sachin Rao: For remediation ideas: 
- Prefer single big kernel for matmul when seq_len > 2k (reduce tail).
- Synthesize KV cache sweeper scheduling into quieter windows (post-response).
- Consider staggered batch windows per worker (randomize alignment) to reduce global bursts.

Mina Patel: Implementation note: the kernel_selector flag is cheap to flip per-model. Staggered windows needs some distribution work in schedule_shards. I'll open a short PR for selector and a perf test comparing window=6|12|18 with and without staggering.

perf-bot: perf-run queued: job/1872 (nsys + perfetto) — results will arrive in ~45m :sparkles:

Jordan Li: Great. One more ask: add a tiny synthetic test that reproduces the batch merge pattern (n_workers=8, poisson arrival with mean inter-arrival=5ms). If we can reproduce offline we can tune heuristics faster.

Mina Patel: Will do. I'll drop traces and a short summary in the perf PR. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
